mainTopic: When the day begins (עמוד השחר), and why daytime מצוות are valid all day, with a source for each one.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous discussion: counting days, like a זבה's count, is done by day. The גמרא then asks for the source of the משנה's rule that daytime מצוות are valid from עמוד השחר. רבא brings a פסוק from בראשית, but the גמרא rejects it, because the same reading would make night start right after sunset. רבי זירא proves it instead from נחמיה, where the work time from dawn until צאת הכוכבים is called 'day'. A new משנה then teaches that the whole day is valid for daytime מצוות such as מגילה, הלל, שופר, לולב, מוסף, the confessions, and the קרבן services. It adds that the whole night is valid for nighttime ones like reaping the עומר. The גמרא goes through the list and gives a source for each item. Some come from a direct 'day' פסוק, some from a גזירה שוה or היקש, and תפילת מוסף follows the מוספין because the רבנן modeled it on them. The amud ends with the source for השקאת סוטה, and the list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Counting days is done in the daytime
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends: a ספירה, a count of clean days, happens by day, so the woman cannot immerse until it is day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Counting is a daytime thing.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the earlier discussion about a woman who must count a clean day. The גמרא gives the reason: counting belongs to the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יום כנגד יום has to count one clean day before she can immerse. Since a counted day is a daytime matter, she must wait until it is day to immerse. Night does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: counting (of clean days)
in the daytime
a woman who must watch one clean day for one day of bleeding

steps.confusionAlert: This line finishes the PREVIOUS topic. It is not part of the new question about עמוד השחר that starts in the next step.

phrases.english: Counting is in the daytime.
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק 'וְסָפְרָה לָּהּ' (she shall count); days are counted in the daytime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion earlier about the זבה's counting.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A count of days, such as a זבה's ספירה, is done by day, so immersion based on it must wait until daytime.

steps.title: משנה: daytime מצוות done from dawn are valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה: all the daytime מצוות listed are valid if done from עמוד השחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them, if they did them from when dawn rose, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the closing rule of the משנה so it can analyze it next. This sets up the question about where the rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed many מצוות that must be done by day, such as reading the מגילה, מילה, and טבילה. The ideal time is from sunrise, but after the fact they work from עמוד השחר, the first light of dawn. So the rule treats dawn as the start of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: the first light of dawn (before sunrise)
valid
and all of them (all the daytime מצוות listed)

phrases.english: And all of them that were done
phrases.notes: Refers to the whole list of daytime מצוות in the משנה.

phrases.english: from when dawn rose — it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִשֶּׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daytime מצוות done from עמוד השחר are valid.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source showing that the day already begins at dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words (derived)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a פסוק that proves dawn already counts as day. The answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the day only starts when the sun comes up. So the גמרא wants a text-based source that the stretch before sunrise is already halachically 'day'.

keyTerms.meaning: from where are these words derived? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source that daytime begins at עמוד השחר.

steps.title: רבא: 'light' means 'getting lighter'
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם' as 'He called the growing light day', so the day begins as soon as it starts getting light.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because the verse says, 'And God called the light day.' That which is becoming lighter and lighter, He called 'day'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question with a פסוק from the creation story in בראשית. He reads the word 'אור' as 'getting lighter'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not read 'אור' as full light. He reads it as the process of light increasing. Since the sky starts brightening at עמוד השחר, that moment is already called 'יום', day.

keyTerms.meaning: because the verse says
to the light
to that which is continuing to grow light
He called it

phrases.english: Rava said: Because the verse says:
"And God called the light day"
That which is getting lighter and lighter, He called "day."
phrases.notes: He's reading 'אור' as light that keeps growing, not light that's already complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with a first source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם', read as 'He called the growing light day', so day begins at first light.

steps.title: Then night would start as it gets dark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבא: by the same reading, 'וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה' would mean night starts as soon as it begins getting dark, yet we hold it is not night until צאת הכוכבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, then 'and the darkness He called night' would mean: that which is getting darker and darker He called night? But we hold that until the stars come out, it is not night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading. It applies his method to the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אור' means 'getting lighter', then 'חשך' should mean 'getting darker'. That would make night begin right after sunset. But the accepted rule is that night only starts at צאת הכוכבים, so this reading of the פסוק cannot be right. That means רבא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so, from now on (introducing an absurd result)
to that which is continuing to grow dark
but we have an established rule
the appearance of the stars (nightfall)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether dawn is day. The problem is that רבא's METHOD of reading the פסוק leads to a wrong result about night. So his source is rejected, even though the משנה's rule still stands.

phrases.english: But if so:
"And the darkness He called night"
[would mean: that which is getting darker and darker He called night]?
phrases.notes: The same way of reading, now used on the word 'חשך'.

phrases.english: But we hold

phrases.aramaic: דְּעַד צֵאת הַכּוֹכָבִים לָאו לַיְלָה הוּא!
phrases.english: that until the stars come out, it is not night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel reading of 'לַחֹשֶׁךְ' would start night at the first darkening after sunset. That contradicts the established rule that night begins at צאת הכוכבים.

steps.title: רבי זירא: proof from the workers in נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a new source from נחמיה: they worked 'from dawn until the stars came out', and the next פסוק calls the night the guard time and the rest day, so dawn is day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: from here: 'And we were doing the work, and half of them held the spears from the rising of dawn until the stars came out.' And it says: 'and the night shall be a guard for us' (and the day for work).
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבא's proof fell away, רבי זירא offers a different source from ספר נחמיה. This is the source the גמרא settles on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says the work lasted from עלות השחר until צאת הכוכבים. The second פסוק sets night as guard time and day as work time. Together they show that the whole work period, starting at dawn, is called 'day'. Without the second פסוק, one could think they simply worked extra hours into the night.

keyTerms.meaning: from here (introducing a new source)
the rising of dawn (same as עמוד השחר)
and it (another verse) says
guard, watch
spears

steps.whatToRemember: The day halachically begins at עמוד השחר and night begins at צאת הכוכבים. The source is רבי זירא's proof from נחמיה, not רבא's reading of בראשית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic boundaries of day and night. Any daytime מצוה, such as מגילה by day or מילה, is valid after the fact from dawn.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said: from here:
"And we were doing the work
and half of them were holding the spears
from the rising of dawn until the stars came out"
And it says: "and the night shall be a guard for us"
phrases.notes: נחמיה ד:טז. The פסוק continues 'and the day for work', which shows the work period from dawn was day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected source with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From נחמיה: work ran from dawn to the stars, and night was for guarding while day was for work, so dawn counts as day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on the first פסוק alone, one might say they worked extra hours into the night.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second פסוק defines night as guard time, so the work period from dawn was day.

steps.title: Why was a second verse needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא added a second פסוק, introduced with 'ואומר' ('and it says'), instead of relying on the first one alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says' (the second verse)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא brought a second פסוק from נחמיה. This question sets up the next step, which explains what the first פסוק alone could not prove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא first quoted 'from dawn until the stars came out' and then added 'and it says' with the next פסוק. The גמרא assumes every extra source must teach something new. So it asks what weakness in the first פסוק the second one fixes.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (Aramaic question word)
'And it says': a formula that adds a second פסוק as further proof

phrases.english: What is the point of 'and it says'?
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי זירא's second פסוק from נחמיה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the structure of רבי זירא's proof in Step 6. It asks why two פסוקים were needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the second פסוק add that the first פסוק could not prove on its own?

steps.title: The second verse shows the whole work time is called day
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק alone could mean the workers simply worked overtime, starting before daytime and continuing after nightfall. The second פסוק calls their whole work period 'day', so dawn really is day.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say that after dawn rises it is still not day, and from sunset it is already night, and they simply started early and stayed late. Come and hear: 'so that the night may be a guard for us and the day for work.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The first פסוק could be explained away, and the second פסוק blocks that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first פסוק alone, one could argue that the workers were extra dedicated. On that reading, they worked from dawn until the stars came out, even though the official day runs only from sunrise to sunset. The second פסוק says that for them 'the night is guard duty and the day is work', so it calls the entire work stretch 'day'. That means the time from dawn counts as day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say': introduces a possible objection
The sun sets
They start early and stay late into the dark
'Come and hear': introduces a proof
Guard duty

steps.whatToRemember: The day begins at עמוד השחר, as proven from נחמיה. The second פסוק is needed so we cannot claim the workers were just working extra hours outside the real day.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
from when dawn rises, it is not yet day,
and from when the sun sets, it is already night,
and they just started early and stayed late into the dark —
phrases.notes: The workers worked beyond the real day.

phrases.english: come and hear:
'so that the night may be a guard for us, and the day for work.'
phrases.notes: נחמיה ד:טז. Their whole work time is called 'day'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מִשֶּׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר לָאו יְמָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 by showing the gap in the first פסוק that the second פסוק fills.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first פסוק could mean the workers worked overtime outside the official day. The second פסוק labels the whole work period 'day', proving that dawn is day.

steps.title: New משנה: the whole day is valid for daytime מצוות
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the whole day is a valid time for reading the מגילה, saying הלל, blowing שופר, taking the לולב, davening מוסף, and bringing the מוספין קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The whole day is valid for reading the מגילה, for reading הלל, for blowing the שופר, for taking the לולב, for the מוסף prayer, and for the מוספין offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists daytime מצוות that can be done at any point during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה taught when daytime מצוות can start, which is from עמוד השחר. This משנה teaches how long the time lasts: the entire day. Doing them early is better, but doing them later in the day is still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: 'our משנה'
Valid, acceptable
Psalms of praise said on holidays
Taking the לולב (with the other species) on סוכות
The extra offerings, and the extra prayer (מוסף), on special days

steps.confusionAlert: 'The whole day' means the daytime only, not the night. This משנה is about how late you can still do these מצוות, while the previous משנה was about how early you can start.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
the whole day is valid for reading the Megillah,
and for reciting Hallel, and for blowing the shofar,
and for taking the lulav,
and for the Musaf prayer, and for the Musaf offerings,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous סוגיא ended. It moves from when the day starts to the fact that the whole day is valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The entire daytime is valid for these daytime מצוות.

steps.title: The whole day is valid for the confessions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. The whole day is also valid for three confessions: over the פרים, over מעשר, and on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the confession over the bulls, and for the declaration about מעשר, and for the confession of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing items with the same rule. It now adds three types of spoken confession or declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are spoken declarations tied to the daytime. The first is the confession over the פרים brought for a mistaken ruling by the סנהדרין or the כהן גדול. The second is the declaration that one's מעשר obligations are complete. The third is the כהן גדול's confession on יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Confession or formal declaration
The bulls brought for a mistaken ruling of the court or the כהן גדול
Declaration that all מעשרות were properly given
The Day of Atonement, when the כהן גדול confesses over the קרבנות

phrases.english: and for the confession over the bulls, and for the tithe declaration,
and for the Yom Kippur confession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list from Step 9 under the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole day is valid for the confession over the פרים, the declaration about מעשר, and the confession of יום הכפורים.

steps.title: The whole day is valid for the Temple services
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds the steps of the קרבן service. The whole day is valid for סמיכה, שחיטה, תנופה, הגשה, קמיצה, הקטרה, מליקה, קבלה, and הזאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For leaning hands, for slaughtering, for waving, for bringing near, for scooping a handful, and for burning, for pinching the neck, and for receiving the blood, and for sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list with the jobs done in the בית המקדש when bringing קרבנות. The list keeps going in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the קרבן services must be done by day. This list teaches that any time during the day works, not only the early morning. Some items belong to animal offerings, some to bird offerings, and some to flour offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before it is offered
Waving certain offerings back and forth
Bringing a flour offering to the corner of the מזבח
Scooping a fistful from a flour offering
Pinching the neck of a bird offering
Sprinkling the blood

phrases.english: for leaning hands, for slaughtering, for waving,
for bringing near, for scooping the fistful, and for burning,
for pinching the bird's neck, and for receiving the blood, and for sprinkling,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list from Steps 9 and 10, now covering the קרבן services.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole day is valid for the daytime עבודות of the קרבנות.

steps.title: Daytime list ends: סוטה, עגלה ערופה, and the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of things valid all day: giving the סוטה the water to drink, breaking the neck of the עגלה ערופה, and purifying the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the whole day is also valid for giving the סוטה the water to drink, for breaking the neck of the calf, and for purifying the מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the last three items to its list of daytime מצוות that can be done any time during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three are special procedures done in front of כהנים or בית דין. They are not ordinary קרבנות, but they are still daytime procedures. Like everything else on the list, they can be done from dawn until sunset, not only in the morning.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman suspected by her husband of being unfaithful, who is given special water to drink
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
The purification process of a person with צרעת

phrases.english: and for giving the סוטה the water to drink,
and for breaking the neck of the calf,
and for the purification of the מצורע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of daytime מצוות from Steps 9–11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving the סוטה the water, the עגלה ערופה, and טהרת המצורע are valid all day long.

steps.title: The nighttime list: עומר, חלבים, and אברים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה now lists מצוות done at night, which are valid all night long: reaping the עומר and burning the fats and limbs of קרבנות on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole night is valid for reaping the עומר, and for burning the fats and the limbs on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches from day to night. It lists מצוות whose time is at night, and says they can be done any time during the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the daytime list. Reaping the עומר happens on the night after the first day of פסח. Fats and limbs left over from the day's קרבנות may be burned on the מזבח all night long.

keyTerms.meaning: Reaping the barley for the עומר offering
Burning the fats of קרבנות on the מזבח
The limbs of a קרבן עולה, burned on the מזבח
The whole night

steps.confusionAlert: Burning the fats and limbs at night does not mean the קרבן was brought at night. The קרבן was brought during the day. Only its leftover parts are burned at night.

phrases.english: The whole night is valid
for reaping the omer,
and for burning fats and limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the nighttime parallel to the daytime list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reaping the עומר and burning חלבים and אברים are valid the entire night.

steps.title: The general rule for day and night
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums everything up: a daytime מצוה is valid all day, and a nighttime מצוה is valid all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: something whose מצוה is by day is valid the whole day. Something whose מצוה is at night is valid the whole night.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with one simple rule that covers both of its lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule goes beyond the listed items. Any מצוה whose time is the day can be done all day, and any מצוה whose time is the night can be done all night. The lists were examples of this principle, not the complete set.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Whose מצוה is during the day

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of the משנה: daytime מצוות are valid all day, and nighttime מצוות are valid all night.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic principle for when many מצוות can be done. For example, you may take a לולב or hear שופר at any time until sunset.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
something whose מצוה is by day —
is valid the whole day.
Something whose מצוה is at night —
is valid the whole night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes both lists in one principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daytime מצוות are valid all day, and nighttime מצוות are valid all night.

steps.title: Where do we know these are daytime מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking for the source that these מצוות belong to the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a short question. It is setting up a series of answers, one פסוק for each מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not about the whole-day rule itself. It asks how we know each of these מצוות is a daytime מצוה in the first place. The answers that follow match a פסוק to each item.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now asks for the source of the משנה's daytime list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that each listed מצוה is done by day.

steps.title: Source for מגילה: 'these days'
steps.stepSummary: Reading the מגילה is by day because the פסוק says 'these days should be remembered and kept.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And these days are remembered and kept.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first source, for reading the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'days', which shows the remembering, meaning the reading, is a daytime מצוה. Whatever is said about the nighttime reading, the main daytime reading follows this rule of 'day'.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the פסוק says
Remembered and kept

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"And these days are remembered and kept."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question for מגילה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מגילה is by day because the פסוק says 'these days' (אסתר ט:כח).

steps.title: Source for הלל: from sunrise to sunset
steps.stepSummary: Saying הלל is by day because הלל itself says 'from the rising of the sun to its setting.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For reading הלל, as it is written: 'From the rising of the sun until its setting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for saying הלל during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes praising ה׳ from sunrise until sunset, which is daytime. So הלל belongs to the day, and the whole day is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Saying הלל
As it is written
From sunrise until sunset

phrases.english: For reading hallel, as it is written:
"From the rising of the sun until its setting."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of sources.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל is by day because of 'ממזרח שמש עד מבואו' (תהלים קיג:ג).

steps.title: רבי יוסי's different source for הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings another פסוק from הלל: 'This is the day that ה׳ made.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: 'This is the day that ה׳ made.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different פסוק for the same point about הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that הלל is said by day. They differ only on which פסוק proves it. רבי יוסי uses a פסוק that says the word 'day' directly.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the day that ה׳ made

phrases.english: (Rabbi Yosei) says:
"This is the day that the Lord has made."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative פסוק for the same law as Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל is by day because of 'זה היום עשה ה׳' (תהלים קיח:כד).

steps.title: Sources for לולב and שופר
steps.stepSummary: לולב is by day because the פסוק says 'on the first day'. שופר is by day because the פסוק says 'a day of תרועה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for taking the לולב, as it is written: 'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day.' And for blowing שופר, as it is written: 'It shall be a day of תרועה for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two more sources, one for לולב and one for שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both פסוקים the key word is 'day' (יום). That word shows the מצוה belongs to the daytime, not the night.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking the לולב
Blowing the שופר
A day of blowing (ראש השנה)

phrases.english: And for taking the lulav, as it is written:
"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day."
And for blowing the shofar, as it is written:
"It shall be a day of sounding for you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues listing sources item by item.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לולב: 'ביום הראשון' (ויקרא כג:מ). שופר: 'יום תרועה' (במדבר כט:א).

steps.title: Source for the מוספין קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The מוספין are brought by day because the פסוק says 'each day's matter on its day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the מוספין, as it is written: 'The matter of each day on its day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for bringing the מוספין קרבנות during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'דבר יום ביומו' ties each קרבן to its own day. That makes it a daytime obligation, valid all day.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra קרבנות brought on שבת, יום טוב, and ראש חודש
Each day's matter on its own day

phrases.english: And for the additional offerings, as it is written:
"The matter of each day on its day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next source in the list.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוספין are by day because of 'דבר יום ביומו' (ויקרא כג:לז).

steps.title: תפילת מוסף follows the מוספין
steps.stepSummary: תפילת מוסף is by day because the רבנן set it up to match the מוספין קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for תפילת המוספין: the רבנן made it like the מוספין.
steps.whatsHappening: The last item has no פסוק of its own. The גמרא explains that תפילת מוסף borrows the rule of the מוספין קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילת מוסף was instituted by the רבנן in place of the מוסף קרבן. So it takes on the קרבן's timing, which is all day. This is a rabbinic link, not a separate פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The מוסף prayer
The רבנן made it equal

steps.whatToRemember: תפילת מוסף has no פסוק of its own. It follows the daytime מוספין קרבנות because the רבנן modeled it on them.

phrases.english: And for the additional prayer —
the Rabbis made it like the additional offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the מוספין source from Step 20 to the תפילה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תפילת מוסף is by day because the רבנן modeled it on the daytime מוספין קרבנות.

steps.title: Confession over the bulls is by day, learned from יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: וידוי פרים is by day. The word כפרה appears both here and by יום הכפורים, so we learn from יום הכפורים. There, כפרה means confession in words, and it happens 'on this day'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And confession over the bulls is by day, because we learn 'atonement' from 'atonement' at יום הכפורים. A ברייתא says about יום הכפורים: 'And he shall atone for himself and for his household.' This verse is talking about atonement through words, meaning confession. And that atonement is by day, as it says: 'On this day He will atone for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the confession said over a bull קרבן must be done by day. It learns this from יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three links. First, a ברייתא shows that 'וכפר' on יום הכפורים means confession in words, not the blood. Second, the פסוק 'ביום הזה יכפר' shows that this כפרה happens by day. Third, a גזירה שוה on the word כפרה carries this daytime rule over to the confession on other bulls.

keyTerms.meaning: The spoken confession said over a bull קרבן
Atonement. This shared word is the link for the גזירה שוה
Atonement through words, meaning confession
By day (Aramaic)
As a ברייתא teaches

steps.confusionAlert: 'וכפר בעדו' might seem to mean the blood service that brings atonement. The ברייתא says it means the spoken confession. That is the only reason this פסוק teaches us about וידוי.

phrases.english: And for the confession over the bulls,
since it learns 'atonement' from 'atonement' at Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word כפרה shows up in both places, linking them.

phrases.english: As it was taught regarding Yom Kippur:
'And he shall atone for himself and for his household'
the verse speaks of atonement through words.
And atonement is by day,
as it is written: 'On this day He will atone for you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list of daytime מצוות
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה כפרה–כפרה from יום הכפורים, where the כפרה is confession and is 'on this day'

steps.title: The declaration about tithes is by day
steps.stepSummary: וידוי מעשר is by day. The פסוק right after the declaration says 'This day ה׳ your God commands you'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the declaration about tithes is by day, because it says: 'And you shall say before ה׳ your God: I have removed the holy things from the house.' Right next to it, the פסוק says: 'This day ה׳ your God commands you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source that וידוי מעשר is said by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration itself does not mention day. But the פסוק placed right after it says 'היום הזה'. The גמרא uses this closeness (סמיכות) to teach that the declaration belongs to the daytime.

keyTerms.meaning: The declaration that all tithes have been properly given out
'I have removed the holy things.' These are the opening words of the declaration
And right next to it. Closeness of פסוקים used to teach something

phrases.english: And for the declaration of tithes, etc.,
as it is written: 'And you shall say before the Lord your God,
I have removed the holy things from the house,'
and juxtaposed to it:
'This day the Lord your God commands you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק next to the declaration says 'היום הזה'

steps.title: Leaning hands and slaughtering are by day
steps.stepSummary: סמיכה is joined to שחיטה in one פסוק. שחיטה is by day because the פסוק says 'on the day you slaughter'. So both are by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Leaning hands and slaughtering are by day, because it says: 'And he shall lean... and slaughter.' And about slaughtering it says: 'On the day of your slaughtering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שחיטה is by day from its own פסוק. Then it attaches סמיכה to שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה has a direct source: 'ביום זבחכם'. סמיכה has no daytime פסוק of its own. Because the פסוק puts 'וסמך' and 'ושחט' side by side, סמיכה follows the same daytime rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the head of the קרבן
Slaughtering the קרבן
'On the day of your slaughtering'

phrases.english: For leaning hands and for slaughtering,
as it is written: 'And he shall lean... and slaughter,'
phrases.notes: The two actions are placed together, so they share one rule

phrases.english: and it is written regarding slaughtering: 'On the day of your slaughtering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שחיטה is by day from 'ביום זבחכם', and סמיכה is joined to it

steps.title: Waving is by day
steps.stepSummary: תנופה is by day because the פסוק says 'on the day you wave the עומר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And waving is by day, as it says: 'On the day you wave the עומר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a direct פסוק showing that תנופה is done by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This one is simple. The word 'ביום' is written right with the waving itself. This step also prepares the next one, because הגשה will be learned from תנופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving parts of a קרבן or a מנחה
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן

phrases.english: And for waving,
as it is written: 'On the day you wave the omer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list

steps.title: Bringing the מנחה near the altar is by day, like waving
steps.stepSummary: הגשה is joined to תנופה in the פסוק about the סוטה's מנחה ('and wave... and bring near'). So it is by day just like waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: And bringing near the altar is by day, because it is joined to waving. It says: 'And the כהן shall take from the woman's hand the מנחת קנאות, and wave... and bring it near.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that הגשה is by day by linking it to תנופה, which was just proven to be by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a היקש: two actions written together in one פסוק share the same rule. Because 'והניף' and 'והקריב' appear together, הגשה takes on the daytime rule of תנופה from step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the מנחה to the corner of the altar
It is joined by a היקש, so it shares the same rule
The 'offering of jealousy' brought by a סוטה

phrases.english: And for bringing near —
since it is likened to waving,
as it is written: 'And the priest shall take from the woman's hand
the meal-offering of jealousy
and wave... and bring it near.'
phrases.notes: Here 'והקריב' means הגשה, bringing the offering close to the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on the תנופה source from the previous step
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש of הגשה to תנופה in the סוטה פסוק

steps.title: Pinching, scooping, burning, and sprinkling are by day
steps.stepSummary: מליקה, קמיצה, הקטרה, and הזיה are all by day. The פסוק about all the קרבנות says 'on the day He commanded בני ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And pinching, scooping, burning, and sprinkling are by day, as it says: 'On the day He commanded בני ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא covers the last group of עבודות in the list with one general פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק (ויקרא ז) closes the whole section on the laws of all types of קרבנות. Its word 'ביום' teaches that the main parts of the קרבן service in general are done by day. So these four items do not each need their own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching the neck of a bird קרבן
Scooping a handful from a מנחה
Burning parts of a קרבן on the altar
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן (on the מזבח or the curtain)

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the confessions and קרבן-service items so far is tied to 'יום' in a פסוק. Sometimes the פסוק is direct (שחיטה, תנופה). Sometimes the link is a גזירה שוה (וידוי פרים), פסוקים placed next to each other (וידוי מעשר), a היקש (סמיכה, הגשה), or one general פסוק (מליקה, קמיצה, הקטרה, הזיה). The next step uses yet another method for סוטה.

phrases.english: And for pinching and for scooping
and for burning and for sprinkling,
as it is written: 'On the day He commanded the children of Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last group of items in the list
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The general פסוק 'ביום צוותו את בני ישראל'

steps.title: Giving the סוטה her drink is by day, learned from the word 'תורה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the source that השקאת סוטה is done by day. The word 'תורה' appears in the סוטה פרשה and in the פסוק about judgment by בית דין. Judgment is by day, so the סוטה process is also by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And giving the סוטה to drink is learned from 'תורה' and 'תורה.' Here, about the סוטה, it says: 'And the כהן shall do to her all this תורה.' And there, about judgment, it says: 'According to the תורה which they shall teach you, and according to the judgment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the next item on its list. It shows why the סוטה must be given the water by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time there is no direct 'on the day' פסוק for the סוטה. So the גמרא uses a גזירה שוה. The word 'תורה' appears in the סוטה פרשה and also in the פסוק about a בית דין's ruling (משפט). That links the two, and since judgment happens by day, the סוטה process must also be by day.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving the suspected woman (סוטה) the bitter water to drink
It comes / it is derived (introduces the source)
Learning one topic from another because the same word appears in both
It is written here... and it is written there (the two sides of a גזירה שוה)
Judgment, a court ruling, which is done by day

steps.confusionAlert: Neither פסוק quoted here actually says the word 'day.' The point is only to link the סוטה to משפט. The 'by day' part comes from the known rule that court judgment happens by day.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a new method in this list. When there is no direct 'day' פסוק, the גמרא connects the מצוה by a shared word to something already known to be done by day.

phrases.english: And for giving the sotah to drink —
it is derived from 'Torah' and 'Torah' (a verbal analogy).
phrases.notes: The same word 'תורה' appears in both places, which creates a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'And the priest shall do to her'
all this Torah,'
and it is written there: 'According to the Torah'
phrases.notes: דברים יז:יא, about the ruling of בית דין

phrases.english: which they shall teach you, and according to the judgment.'
phrases.notes: Since judgment (משפט) is done by day, the סוטה process is also by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources for the 'by day' מצוות. Earlier steps used direct 'on the day' פסוקים. This one uses a גזירה שוה instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that השקאת סוטה must be done by day?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'תורה' links the סוטה to court judgment (משפט). Judgment is by day, so השקאת סוטה is by day too.
